NASA Image The Houthis are claiming an attack on a Dutch cargo ship that resulted in a fire and left two crew members injured. The Yemen-based group used a cruise missile to attack M/V Minervagracht , a ship managed by Dutch company Spliethoff, while it was in the Gulf of Aden, Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Sare’e posted on X late Tuesday. Spliethoff confirmed the Houthi attack, reporting that the ship caught fire and the crew was evacuated by helicopter to nearby vessels, where the two injured mariners received first aid. The company is working with international authorities and towage experts to secure the ship, according to a company statement. At the time of the attack, the ship was sailing eastbound from Djibouti, Africa. The ship was not carrying any cargo, according to the company. “Finally, we would again like to express our deepest concern over this week’s incident, which was a direct attack on our innocent seafarers and a breach of the right of free navigation,” reads the statement from Spliethoff on the incident. The Houthis claimed they attacked Minervagracht because the owner violated their ban on port visits to Israel. The Netherlands called on the European Union to sanction the Houthis as a terrorist organization as a result of the attack, Reuters reported. This is the first time the Houthis have retaliated against a ship since July, with the Yemen-based group focusing their efforts on attacking Israel directly. In July, the Houthis attacked two Greek-owned commercial ships sailing under Liberian flags. The group claimed the owners of the ships had also violated its ban on visiting Israeli ports. The Houthis first attacked M/V Magic Seas with small boats and then with ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones. The crew abandoned the ship . The next day, the Houthis entered into a 16-hour battle with the crew of M/V Eternity C, which resulted in the death of four crew members and the sinking of the ship. The Houthis captured six members of the crew. Another nine died in the sinking. A merchant vessel rescued the remaining members of the 22-person crew. The Houthis announced in late July that the group would target any ship that visited Israel, although it did not follow through on its threat until the attack on Minervagracht. Unlike the Houthi attacks of 2024 and early 2025, the last three resulted in significant damage to ships. The U.S. reduced operations in the Red Sea after May following the end of Operation Rough Rider, which saw aggressive attacks on the Houthis’ leadership and infrastructure. As of Monday, the U.S. has two destroyers — USS Forrest Sherman (DDG-98) and USS Mitscher (DDG-57) — in the Red Sea, according to USNI News’ Fleet and Marine Tracker .
